content: 1. Recent studies by Xiao S et al. have explored the potential of artemether as an innovative agent for preventing schistosomiasis japonica, mansoni, and haematobia. These findings were published in Acta Tropica in 2002. 2. Grace C. analyzed the impact of evolving intellectual property laws on the pharmaceutical industry in India and China, with a focus on access to medicines. This report was accessed on March 2, 2012. 3. Tanner M, Kitua A, and Degremont AA documented the development of health research capabilities in Tanzania, transitioning from the Swiss Tropical Institute Field Laboratory to the Ifakara Centre of the Tanzanian National Institute of Medical Research. This work was published in Acta Tropica in 1994. 4. Ofori-Adjei D emphasized the importance of investing in health research for endemic diseases in the Ghana Medical Journal in 2008. 5. The WHO Technical Report Series No. 972 (2012) outlined research priorities for helminth infections, as determined by the TDR Disease Reference Group on Helminth Infections. 6. Bonfoh B et al. discussed the challenges of conducting research in war zones, as published in Nature in 2011. 7. Guidelines for conducting research in partnership with developing countries were established, emphasizing ethical collaboration and mutual benefit. These principles were accessed on March 2, 2012. 8. Bethony JM and Loukas A reviewed the current research agenda for schistosomiasis and proposed future directions in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2008. 9. Young J and Kannemeyer N conducted a study to map existing initiatives for building research capacity in Southern regions. 10. Binka F, in an editorial published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2005, advocated for equitable North-South research collaborations. 11. The Abuja Declaration addressed the urgent need to combat HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and other infectious diseases, with the document accessed on March 2, 2012. 12. The Algiers Declaration (June 2008) focused on narrowing the knowledge gap to improve health outcomes in Africa. 13. The Bamako Call to Action emphasized strengthening research for health, development, and equity, with the document accessed on March 2, 2012. 14. The Commission on Health Research for Development highlighted the essential role of health research in achieving equity in development, as published by Oxford University Press in 1990. 15. The World Bank's Accra Agenda for Action outlined strategies for improving global health research and development. 16. Utzinger J and Keiser J reviewed common drugs used for the treatment and control of schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminthiasis in Expert Opinion in Pharmacotherapy in 2004. 17. Fürst T, Keiser J, and Utzinger J conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the global burden of human food-borne trematodiasis, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2012. 18. Utzinger J proposed a research and development agenda for the control and elimination of human helminthiases in an editorial in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2012. 19. Lustigman S et al. outlined a research agenda for helminth diseases, focusing on basic research and enabling technologies to support control and elimination efforts, as published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2012. 20. McCarthy JS et al. emphasized the need for improved diagnostics for helminth diseases to enhance control and elimination programs, as detailed in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2012. 21. Osei-Atweneboana MY et al. highlighted the importance of health research and capacity building in disease-endemic countries for helminthiasis control, as published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2012. 22. The WHO Technical Report Series No. 972 (2012) provided a comprehensive overview of research priorities for helminth infections, as determined by the TDR Disease Reference Group. 23. Annexes in the report detailed the composition of thematic and disease-specific reference groups, their leadership, and the top ten research priorities for helminthiases. These priorities included optimizing existing intervention tools, developing novel control tools, improving diagnostic tests, and refining models to assess the relationship between infection and morbidity. 24. The report emphasized the interconnected nature of these research priorities, which must be addressed simultaneously to achieve sustainable progress in controlling helminth infections.
